description.value: The study assessed the effects of a single session of exercise versus passive control on regional brain activation during viewing of smoking-related stimuli in abstinent smokers, and examined cigarette cravings.

spans.text: The primary aim of this study was to assess the effects of a single session of exercise (versus a passive control condition) on regional brain activation while viewing smoking-related stimuli in an event-related fMRI study.

description.value: Randomized crossover design with exercise and passive control conditions; participants abstained from smoking overnight and were scanned after each condition.

source_definition.value: Experimental treatment condition with two levels: passive control (10 minutes of passive sitting) and exercise (2-minute warm-up followed by 10 minutes of cycling at RPE 11–13).

spans.text: The control condition involved sitting passively in the laboratory without access to reading materials, mobile phone, or internet for 10 min.

hrf_model.value: Canonical hemodynamic response function with no time derivative.

spans.text: Event types were modeled for each subject (fixation, non-smoking, and smoking) using a canonical hemodynamic (hrf) with no time derivative.

model_settings.value: Subject-level event types (fixation, non-smoking, and smoking) were modeled with a general linear model; images were realigned, normalized, slice-timed, and smoothed to 6 mm. A 128-second high-pass filter and global correction were applied. First-level contrast images were entered into random-effects second-level one-sample t tests comparing control and exercise conditions.

software.value: SPM2 (Statistical Parametric Mapping), with analyses conducted using one-sample t tests at the random-effects second level.
